Only methods declared in sugar-panels/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

SugarCraft\Panels

Node final class

Immutable layout tree node.

MethodSummary
static leaf(string|Buffer $content = ''): selfA leaf paints either text or pre-built cells. Text is the historical door: it is sanitized at the paint boundary and word-wrapped into the region. A Buffer is placed cell for cell (each cell keeps its own pen, link and width), so a host that already renders into cells does not have to flatten them into escape strings for the panel to re-parse.
static horizontal(Node ...$children): self
static vertical(Node ...$children): self
static noBorder(Node $child): selfNo-border wrapper — suppresses every frame and every divider through the whole subtree, so adjacent panels render touching. Contrast with self::withBorder(false), which hides one node's own frame and leaves the rest of the layout's rules in place. The wrapper carries border:false and threads $noFrames on render (see SugarPanels::renderNoBorder; pinned by tests/FramingAndSeparatorsTest.php).
isLeaf(): boolShape predicates. The kind string constants remain the wire form, but comparisons are spelled through these so intent reads and the constants cannot be hand-typo'd at call sites.
isHorizontal(): bool
isVertical(): bool
withMinWidth(int $w): self
withMaxWidth(int $w): self
withMinHeight(int $h): self
withMaxHeight(int $h): self
withFlex(int $weight): selfMark this child as flexible: in a horizontal/vertical parent it grows to fill the space left after the fixed (non-flex) siblings take their natural size, sharing that leftover with other flex children in proportion to the weight. A weight of 0 means the child is fixed (non-flex).
withGrow(): selfShorthand for withFlex(1): this child fills the leftover space.
withPadding(int $cells): selfInner inset around painted content. Applies to leaf nodes only; a container ignores it — its children fill the box.
withBorder(bool $show): selfToggle this node's OWN frame. Contrast with self::noBorder(), which flattens a whole subtree's frames and dividers, while this hides only the one box and leaves sibling frames and rules alone. The chosen border style survives a true → false → true round-trip: disabling hides the frame, enabling re-shows the style that was last set.
withSpacing(int $cells): self
withBorderStyle(?Border $b): selfSet the border character set from sugar-style. Passing null CLEARS the style: the frame then falls back to Border::rounded() at draw time. The border bool still controls visibility — clearing the style does not hide the border.
withStyle(?Style $s): selfSet the canonical style from sugar-style. Passing null CLEARS the style — content renders unstyled.
withTitle(string $t): selfSet the box title text. Passing '' CLEARS the title — the top edge renders as an unbroken run.
withMargin(int $top, ?int $right = null, ?int $bottom = null, ?int $left = null): selfSet outer margin (top, right, bottom, left). sugar-panels-specific: sugar-style Style does not ship margin as a first-class concept.
withAlignH(?Align $a): selfSet horizontal text alignment (sugar-panels-specific). Passing null CLEARS the alignment — content renders left-aligned.
withAlignV(?VAlign $v): selfSet vertical text alignment (sugar-panels-specific). Passing null CLEARS the alignment — content renders top-aligned.
withContent(string $content): selfPainted string for a leaf. Containers paint their children, never a content string, so content set on a container is stored but inert.
withCells(?Buffer $cells): selfCells for a leaf to paint instead of its text content. While cells are set they win over $content; passing null returns the leaf to its text. Cells are placed top-left in the padded content box and clipped to it; leaf style and alignment apply to text only.
withScrollOffset(int $rows): selfSkip this many rows of leaf content from the top (text rows after word wrap, or cell rows). Negative values clamp to 0. At render time the offset also clamps to the last full page, so scrolling past the end shows the final rows instead of an empty box.
withFocused(bool $focused = true): selfMark this node as focused: its frame paints with the focus border set (withFocusBorderStyle(), default Border::thick()) and the focus pen (withFocusStyle()). A node whose frame is hidden has no focus frame to show. Layout is unchanged: focus never moves a cell.
withFocusBorderStyle(?Border $border): selfBorder set for the focus frame; null restores Border::thick().
withFocusStyle(?Style $style): selfPen for the focus frame glyphs; null paints them unstyled.
totalWidth(): intTotal width including border, padding, the node's own left+right margin, and — for HORIZONTAL layouts only — the inter-child spacing. Vertical spacing consumes rows, never columns, so it is excluded from the width footprint (mirroring totalHeight()'s treatment of horizontal spacing).
totalHeight(): int
marginWidth(): intThe node's own horizontal margin (left + right).
marginHeight(): intVertical counterpart of marginWidth(): top + bottom.

Sanitize final class

The paint boundary: what a panel is willing to place into a cell grid.

MethodSummary
static painted(string $text): stringNormalise text destined for the grid into text the grid can paint.
static paintedTitle(string $title): stringNormalise a box title.

Splitter final class

A run of panes split along one axis with draggable dividers.

MethodSummary
static horizontal(Node ...$panes): selfPanes side by side; dividers are vertical and drag by column.
static vertical(Node ...$panes): selfPanes stacked top to bottom; dividers are horizontal and drag by row.
withPanes(Node ...$panes): selfReplace the panes. Sizes survive when the pane count is unchanged; otherwise the span is shared out again equally.
withBounds(int $x, int $y, int $width, int $height): selfWhere the splitter is painted, in screen cells. Existing sizes are rescaled proportionally to the new span (equal shares when none were set), so a terminal resize keeps the split's proportions.
withSizes(int ...$sizes): selfSet the pane sizes explicitly (cells along the axis). The list is fitted to the span: a short or long total is rescaled, and no pane goes below the minimum while the span can hold every pane at the minimum. Called before withBounds() (no span yet), the list is kept and fitted once bounds arrive, so the call order does not matter.
withMinPaneSize(int $cells): selfSmallest size a drag may leave a pane with (clamped to at least 1).
withDividerDrag(int $position, ?int $divider = null): selfMove a divider so it lands on screen column (row, for a vertical splitter) $position.
dividerAt(int $col, int $row): ?intWhich divider sits at screen cell ($col, $row), or null. Divider i is the last column (row) of pane i, across the splitter's full cross extent.
dividerPositions(): arrayScreen column (row) of each divider, in order.
isDragging(): bool
update(Msg $msg): arrayDrive divider drag from mouse messages.
node(): NodeThe layout tree for the current sizes: a frameless, spacing-0 container whose panes are weighted by their sizes, so SugarPanels gives each pane exactly its cells when the tree is rendered at the splitter's span. A pane's own flex weight is cleared and its min* along the axis becomes its size (the splitter owns that axis). Before bounds are known the panes are returned unweighted.

SugarPanels final class

Box-drawing layout renderer.

MethodSummary
static new(): selfCreate a new SugarPanels instance — the canonical door (mirrors the house ::new() factory convention Node follows). It is sugar over the identical public constructor below; both are documented at self::__construct().
__construct()Create a new SugarPanels instance.
leaf(string|Buffer $content = ''): NodeA leaf of text, or of pre-built cells (see Node::leaf()).
horizontal(Node ...$children): Node
vertical(Node ...$children): Node
noBorder(Node $child): Node
render(Node $root, int $width, int $height): stringRender a layout node tree into a string within the given viewport.
paintedLeaves(): intHow many leaves the last render() painted.
resetPreviousFrame(): voidReset the previous-frame buffer, forcing the next render to emit a full frame (used on window resize or cursor-position-lost events).
